name: one photo card pulls back into a full batch grid
looks: A single small photo card sits centred. The camera pulls back and the card turns out to be one tile among dozens, all tilted slightly in a dense mosaic of portraits, food, streets and products, every tile already carrying its own finished edit. A kinetic two-word line cuts across the middle of the grid as it settles.
build: Absolutely positioned DOM tiles in one large world; a pseudo-camera move (focus + log scale) pulls back from one tile's full-bleed framing to the whole grid, each tile's corner radius and rotation settling as it reaches its slot. The headline is a single hard-cut DOM block layered over the grid, no per-letter stagger.
sound: A rising whoosh through the pull-back, a soft cluster of ticks as the grid resolves, a hit under the headline.
prompt: Pull the camera back from one finished result until it turns out to be a single tile in a dense grid of many, each already carrying its own result. Land a short, bold two-word claim across the middle of the grid as the pull-back settles, to sell scale rather than one example.
